greece.text: A Phoenician captain told me silver is selling for a fortune in Tyre this season. The temples there demand it for votive offerings.
Word from the docks: Alexandrian grain ships haven't arrived in weeks. Wheat prices in Athens are climbing fast.
A merchant from Syracuse says Sicilian wine is flowing cheap this year. Good vintage, they say.
Sailors speak of Egyptian papyrus being scarce — the Nile floods were poor. Scribes in Athens pay dearly for it.
I overheard that bronze from Cyprus is cheap right now. The mines at Kition are producing more than the smiths can work.
They say Corinthian pottery workshops are idle — too many pots, not enough buyers. A shrewd trader could fill a hold cheaply.
A Cretan sailor mentioned that Tyrian purple is fetching outrageous prices in Rome. Senators pay anything for that color.
Garum from Gadir is the talk of every port tavern. The Iberians make the finest fish sauce, and Egypt craves it.

levant.text: A caravan driver says olive oil is scarce in Memphis. The Egyptian priests need it for temple lamps.
Phoenician glass is selling well in Greece. The Athenians love our translucent vessels.
Ships from Iberia bring word: silver from the western mines is flooding the market. Prices there are very low.
The temples in Byblos are paying well for spices. Frankincense for the rituals of Baal, they say.
A Rhodian merchant told me textiles are cheap in Miletos. The weavers there have had a productive season.
Cedar timber from these mountains fetches a king's ransom in treeless Egypt. The pharaohs need it for their ships.
I hear the Carthaginians are buying up all the grain they can find. Preparing for something, no doubt.
A sailor from Salamis says Cypriot bronze is cheap as dirt. Every mine on the island is working double.

egypt.text: Greek traders in the harbor say Athens pays handsomely for our papyrus. Their philosophers consume scrolls like bread.
A Phoenician captain warns that spice caravans from Arabia have been raided. Spice prices are rising everywhere.
Wine from Massalia is particularly fine this year, and they're selling cheap to undercut the Greeks.
I heard Lepcis Magna has surplus grain from a good harvest. A trader could buy low there.
The silphium from Cyrenaica grows rarer each year. Any merchant with silphium can name their price in Greece.
Pottery from Athens commands respect here. Our nobles love the painted scenes of Greek heroes.
The Sidonians have perfected a new glassblowing technique. Their wares are the finest — and the cheapest — in years.
Gadir's garum is said to fetch double its weight in silver when sold in Ostia. The Romans are mad for it.

north_africa.text: Merchants from the east say bronze is in short supply around Byzantion. The Thracian mines are exhausted.
I hear textiles from Tyre are cheap now. The dye-works are overproducing to compete with Egyptian linen.
Grain ships heading to Athens fetch good prices. The city always needs more than it grows.
Silver from the Laurion mines near Athens is being sold cheaply. A good time to buy and sell east.
A trader from Ostia says Rome devours olive oil faster than Greece can produce it. Good margins there.
Timber is scarce in our ports. Any captain bringing cedar from Byblos would be welcomed warmly.
The Sicilians have wine to spare. Syracuse practically gives it away at the docks.
Word is that papyrus prices in Naukratis have dropped. The scribes there have more than they can use.

italy.text: Egyptian grain is the lifeblood of Rome. Any captain bringing wheat to Ostia will find eager buyers.
A Carthaginian trader says silphium is nearly impossible to find. If you spot any, buy it — it sells for a fortune.
Iberian silver is flooding western markets. Emporion is the place to buy it cheap.
The Phoenicians in Sidon have glassware of extraordinary quality. Cheap there, dear everywhere else.
Spice merchants from the east say pepper and cinnamon are scarce this season. Prices in Tyre are climbing.
Purple dye from Tyre is always in demand here. Roman nobles will pay anything to wear the imperial color.
I heard that Knossos has fine wine at bargain prices. The Cretans had an excellent harvest.
A Greek sailor says Attic pottery sells well in Carthage. The North Africans prize it highly.

iberia.text: Phoenician traders say olive oil is expensive in Egypt. They cannot get enough of it for their temples.
Silver from our mines sells for triple its cost when shipped to Tyre. The Phoenicians value it highly.
A Greek merchant told me textiles are cheap in Ephesos. The Ionian weavers had a good year.
Garum from our coast is the finest in the world, and Rome cannot get enough. Ostia pays well.
I hear bronze tools fetch high prices in Sparta. Their army always needs more.
Egyptian papyrus is hard to find out here. If you bring scrolls from Alexandria, scholars will pay handsomely.
Wine from Rhodes is said to be the best value this year. The Rhodians are eager to sell.
A Carthaginian captain says wheat from Utica is cheap and plentiful after their harvest.
